properties.name: Installing reflow2 into a project leaves a committable design record in the repo — the artifact teammates read
properties.statement:
ANTHONY, 2026-08-13, after Alex's first run on a real work project: *"this is a core feature of reflow2. both my brother and I thought it already worked."*

**IT DID NOT, AND IT NEVER HAD.** `git log -S "docs/design" -- tools/reflow2_init.py` returns exactly ONE commit — the one that fixed it. The same for any non-backup export destination. So this is NOT the regression it felt like: nothing was lost, and there was never a working version to lose.

🛑 THE REASON IT WAS INVISIBLE, AND IT IS THE WHOLE POINT OF WRITING THIS DOWN: **no Requirement and no Capability ever said it.** A search of every Requirement and Capability for *durable record / committed export / shareable / docs/design* returns nothing about a consumer's committable record; the nearest, `req:design-reachable-without-the-repo`, is about reaching a design WITHOUT the repo, which is a different need.

⇒ CONSEQUENCES, ALL OF WHICH ARE THE SYSTEM WORKING CORRECTLY:
  · `cap:kit` reads `verified` and is NOT lying — its scope is *"one command sets up or refreshes the design environment"*, which it does.
  · `detect_gaps` could not surface it. It finds Requirements nothing satisfies; **it cannot find a Requirement nobody wrote.**
  · Every gate was green and every gate was right.

⇒ **AN UNSTATED REQUIREMENT CANNOT BE UNMET.** That is the one class reflow2 is structurally blind to, and it produced a hole in the feature the whole tool exists for: the design record other people read.

📌 WHAT THE INSTALLER DID INSTEAD, which is why two users believed it worked: it DID export — `backup_graph` writes `.reflow2/backups/design-<stamp>.json` — and `git check-ignore` confirms that path is covered by the `.gitignore` rule THE SAME INSTALLER WRITES. **The output of the one export landed inside the ignore rule.** Everything looked present and nothing was reachable.

⚠️ AND THE PROTECTION THREAD WOULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT IT. `dec:idea-a-satisfied-requirement-earns-a-stricter-mutability-class` and `dec:idea-stability-is-earned-by-history-not-by-reaching-a-state` both protect what IS recorded — a satisfied requirement, an operational thread, a stable lifecycle. Alex's *"don't change core functionality"* is about DRIFT. This was ABSENCE from the first commit, so freezing, scoring or baselining would have left it exactly as open. **The measure this needs is different in kind, and confusing the two would build the wrong safeguard.**

WHAT THE REQUIREMENT IS, stated so it can be checked: after `reflow2_init.py` runs, the project contains a design export at a path git will track — `docs/design/<project>.json` — and the user is told, where they are looking, that this is the file to commit. It must hold on a BRAND-NEW project, which is the only case either user actually hit.

📌 EVIDENCE CLASS WORTH NOTING: both of Alex's reports (`fact:second-user-report-2026-08-11`, `fact:second-user-first-run-report-2026-08-13`) were found by somebody meeting the output for the first time, and neither was visible to anyone who already knew the system. That is now two data points for the same instrument.
